meta.title: The Rollback Loop
meta.subtitle: Restore, replay, carry on — the same machine every frame, whether or not anything went wrong

views.label: Where the loop starts
views.note: The oldest prediction start tick across every predicted ghost decides how far back the whole loop rewinds.

views.label: The inner loop
views.note: One iteration per tick. The Simulate bit decides which entities latch this edge.

views.label: There is no compare
views.note: Nothing checks whether the prediction was right. The server state is written over it either way.

views.label: When nothing arrives
views.note: With no new snapshot the loop restarts from its own last full tick, so it keeps running on faith.

cards.title: The loop, stated as a machine
items: Set the program counter to the oldest prediction start tick of any predicted ghost
For each tick up to the target: enable Simulate on whoever should run, execute one tick
After the last full tick, copy the result into the backup
Repeat next frame — this runs whether or not anything was mispredicted

cards.title: There is no compare in the hot path
items: Nothing branches on prediction was right versus wrong
The server's fields are written over the predicted ones every time
If the prediction was correct the write changes nothing, and costs the same
Comparison exists only for smoothing and for the debug system's error metric

cards.title: The bit that eats projects
items: Simulate is enabled per entity per replayed tick, not once per frame
A query without it integrates every predicted entity on every iteration
Ten replayed ticks then move the capsule ten times too far
It looks perfect on a clean link and disintegrates on the first dropped packet

cards.title: The cost, and the two valves
items: Cost is replayed ticks × predicted entities × your predicted systems
Replayed ticks come from round trip time; you do not control that
Predicted entities you do control, and it is the only honest lever
Batching replayed ticks is the emergency valve and it changes the result
